core_obligations: Read the data (proof lines 5959-5967): start with an etale V over Y, an etale covering {U_i -> X x_Y V} and a point v of V, so that the assumption of property (B) is in force.

Use finiteness of the fibre (proof lines 5970-5990): since X x_Y V -> V is finite, its fibre over v consists of finitely many pairwise distinct points x_1, ..., x_n, which makes the local analysis finite.

Apply property (A) at each point (proof lines 5993-6023): for each l choose an index i_l and a point u_l of U_{i_l} mapping to x_l, and apply the companion property for finite morphisms at these points to produce an etale neighbourhood of v and the disjoint union decomposition required by property (B).
proof_roadmap: Start from the data of property (B) for a finite morphism f : X -> Y.
Finiteness of the base change makes the fibre over the given point finite.
Apply the companion property for finite morphisms at the finitely many points of the fibre.
Assemble the resulting local decomposition into the disjoint union decomposition required for property (B).
difficulty_reason: The lemma verifies property (B) for a finite morphism of schemes (statement lines 5953-5957, with property (B) itself delivered verbatim as a context span from lines 5935-5947 because the statement refers to it by name). The proof combines two inputs: finiteness of the base change X x_Y V -> V, which makes the fibre over the given point v consist of finitely many points (proof lines 5970-5990), and the companion property for finite morphisms, applied at the points of that fibre (proof lines 5993-6023), which produces the etale neighbourhood and the disjoint union decomposition demanded by property (B). The non-formal content is the assembly of the finitely many local decompositions into the single neighbourhood required. The claim is H2: a short argument whose work is the finite bookkeeping over the fibre.
